cells.tense: You're standing in the middle of what you understand, and there's nothing left to look for.
cells.ask: when you have seen something whole, say the whole of it to one person before you trim it down — and let that person help you put it down.
cells.core:
This is what it looks like when the holding is going well: you take in a situation complete, all of it at once, and you can carry that while you keep moving. Someone brings you a mess and you already know its shape. You don't have to squint, wait for more, or brace. The seeing and the carrying run together, and the people around you lean on it without either of you making a thing of it.

Hand the whole of what you see to one person. Not the trimmed version, not the one built to be easy to hear — the full shape of it, said to someone standing near you. The weight is real either way. Said out loud, some of it moves across to them, and you get to keep walking.
cells.sheetLine: You see it whole, you keep carrying it, and you haven't handed the seeing to anyone yet.
cells.verb: seeing the whole of a thing at once, with nothing left hidden
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and carries under weight

cells.tense: You're bracing for the last part before it's here, already decided how this has to end.
cells.ask: begin one thing today with no idea where it's going — just the first motion, before it has a direction — and let that be the whole of what you asked of yourself.
cells.core:
Seeing the whole of a thing is your strength, but right now you're living in a version of it that hasn't happened. You've worked out how the rest of this goes, so you're holding yourself against a future that hasn't arrived, carrying weight for a load no one handed you. The clear sight that usually steadies you has turned into certainty about what's coming, and the carrying has become bracing.

Start something without knowing where it will land. Not a plan, not a finished thought — movement with no direction yet, and nothing in you asking it to prove itself. Everything is fresh for a minute, and that's all it needs to be.
cells.sheetLine: You've already decided how this ends and you're carrying it before it's here.
cells.verb: seeing the whole of a thing at once, with nothing left hidden
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and carries under weight

cells.tense: You got to the end of it and stopped, and you're still standing where you stopped.
cells.ask: put one thing into form today — write it, say it, make the shape of it concrete — from what you can actually see now, not what you knew then.
cells.core:
This capacity is meant to finish something and then let the finishing move you. When it's working, you understand a thing completely and that understanding sends you forward — you hold it and walk with it at the same time, and the people around you feel the steadiness of someone who knows what they're carrying and where they're going.

The seeing got done. At some point back there you finished understanding something, and instead of that being the start of anything, it became a place you sat down. You're still carrying it, but you're not moving from it, and the carrying has gone quiet. What's missing isn't insight. It's the step where one clear thing becomes a direction — a single concrete move made now, from what's in front of you rather than what was decided before.
cells.sheetLine: You understand it completely and you haven't moved since.
cells.verb: seeing the whole of a thing at once, with nothing left hidden
cells.place: in the part of you that holds and carries under weight

cells.tense: You're seeing all of it — the whole picture, clearly — and you're talking about it as if someone else drew it.
cells.ask: say "I see this whole" about one thing you're talking about as if it just happened to be clear — claim the seeing as yours.
cells.core:
When this is going well, the holding and the seeing are one motion: you read what's in front of you completely, carry it without strain, and everyone in the room can feel that you know exactly what's here. That steadiness is the whole point of it — not bracing, not effort, just a clear eye that lets you stand under real weight without going stiff.

You already read the room. You know how it fits together, you hold each situation complete before anyone else has spoken — and you describe it as just how things are. Say the seeing is yours. It's the same ability, only now it's held by the person it belongs to. That's the whole move: not more work, just the claim.
cells.sheetLine: You're seeing it whole and calling it things simply being clear.
